correlation_note: The customers-table pull in access-log.txt used exactly this gap — RLS was off, so the service-role key (or even the anon key) was sufficient.

findings.title: customers table: Row-Level Security never enabled
findings.detail: Scaffolded by Lovable without RLS turned on. Same root cause pattern as CVE-2025-48757 (Lovable, 170+ apps affected) and the Moltbook breach (1.5M tokens, 35K emails exposed).
findings.recommended_fix: Enable RLS on every table at creation time, not as an afterthought. Lovable has since made this the default — confirm your project's migrations actually reflect the current default.

findings.title: tickets table: RLS enabled but policy is USING (true)
findings.detail: Technically 'has RLS' but the policy matches every row for every requester — functionally identical to no RLS. A schema diff or migration review that only checks rowsecurity=true would miss this.
findings.recommended_fix: Review policy EXPRESSIONS, not just whether RLS is toggled on. Scope to auth.uid()/org membership like ticket_comments already does correctly.
